8: Iteration 5 starts from the child's two BUB1B alleles and the BubR1 protein instead of from drug databases, in four routes run as one step, each licensed by a positive control declared in writing before the child's data were touched. R1 (allele-specific): the stop_gained allele's context was derived from the public gene model - a UGA stop with a +4 A in exon 17 of 23, 746 nt upstream of the last exon-exon junction, so nonsense-mediated decay destroys the message, and the entire protein-kinase domain is lost. A group-mean context model over 5,837 measured pathogenic premature stops x 8 compounds (Toledano 2024, PMID 39174735) predicts readthrough for this exact context; its held-out control (14 benchmark stops, plus a random fifth, bar rho >= 0.5 and pairwise ordering >= 0.7 fixed before the run) passes for 2,6-diaminopurine, G418 and SRI-41315, fails for five other compounds, and correctly fails for the untreated column. A dosage model then prices each lever in percent of wild-type BubR1: readthrough is worth at most about 1.4 points against a roughly 6.5-point gap, while doubling the missense protein is worth 12.5, so the missense allele is the lever and the aminoglycoside class is ruled out twice (predicted effect at the assay floor for this context, and nephrocalcinosis in the child's own terms). R2 (protein level): in drug-perturbation proteomics (Mitchell 2023, 875 compounds x 9,714 proteins; ProTargetMiner), BUB1B protein is 99.7th-percentile proliferation-bound, so a proliferation score is regressed out and the robust z of the residual ranked. The gating control (HSP90 inhibition raising HSPA1A) ranks 1 and 2 of 875. Five approved corrected risers move BubR1 by only 14-16 percent; the strongest raisers are a CDK1 inhibitor and a proteasome inhibitor, pointing at degradation. Re-running iteration 4's LINCS reversal with the cell-cycle component removed still fails its checkpoint-sibling control, so no reverser list was produced; TTK is the one sibling that survives. R3 (literature as a data source): 6 topic queries written without naming any paper retrieved 767 papers; a lexical screen selected sentences; a reader wrote structured intervention and exposure rows; then code, not the model, verified that every quoted sentence appears verbatim in the cached text of the cited paper. Recall 3/3 on both halves; 42 of 42 rows verified. R4 (decision and value of information) weighs the routes per branch and prices the lab test that separates them. 14: Loss of function, hypomorphic, of a compound heterozygote confirmed by the challenge's answer key: one stop_gained and one missense allele in BUB1B. Iteration 5 characterises the two alleles separately. The stop allele is a UGA premature termination codon with a +4 A in exon 17 of 23, 746 nucleotides upstream of the last exon-exon junction, therefore competent for nonsense-mediated decay: its message is destroyed and no truncated protein accumulates, and the truncation would in any case remove the entire protein-kinase domain (UniProt 766-1050). It is effectively a null. The missense allele keeps a normal message and, in published MVA patient cells, a protein present at a two- to six-fold reduced level whose activity is restored by forced overexpression, so the functional deficit is one of protein amount rather than protein quality - the hypomorphic half of the genotype. Pathway disrupted: the spindle assembly checkpoint, in which BubR1 is part of the mitotic checkpoint complex. Downstream consequence: chromosome mis-segregation and mosaic aneuploidy, with early senescence, muscle wasting and growth failure in the corresponding mouse hypomorph, matching the child's clinical terms. The fork iteration 5 cannot close from public data is whether the missense protein is unstable (degraded fast) or inactive (stable but broken); a cycloheximide-chase measurement in patient cells separates them.
